original_value: Unmanned aerial systems (UASs) have recently been proven to be valuable remote sensing tools for detecting marine macro litter (MML), with the potential of supporting pollution monitoring programs on coasts. Very low altitude images, acquired with a low-cost RGB camera onboard a UAS on a sandy beach, were used to characterize the abundance of stranded macro litter. We developed an object-oriented classification strategy for automatically identifying the marine macro litter items on a UAS-based orthomosaic. A comparison is presented among three automated object-oriented machine learning (OOML) techniques, namely random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and k-nearest neighbor (KNN). Overall, the detection was satisfactory for the three techniques, with mean F-scores of 65% for KNN, 68% for SVM, and 72% for RF. A comparison with manual detection showed that the RF technique was the most accurate OOML macro litter detector, as it returned the best overall detection quality (F-score) with the lowest number of false positives. Because the number of tuning parameters varied among the three automated machine learning techniques and considering that the three generated abundance maps correlated similarly with the abundance map produced manually, the simplest KNN classifier was preferred to the more complex RF. This work contributes to advances in remote sensing marine litter surveys on coasts, optimizing the automated detection on UAS-derived orthomosaics. MML abundance maps, produced by UAS surveys, assist coastal managers and authorities through environmental pollution monitoring programs. In addition, they contribute to search and evaluation of the mitigation measures and improve clean-up operations on coastal environments.

result.paraphrase: Unmanned aerial systems (UASs) have recently been shown to be useful remote-sensing tools for detecting marine macro litter (MML), with potential to support coastal pollution monitoring programs. Very low-altitude images taken over a sandy beach using a low-cost RGB camera mounted on a UAS were used to characterize the abundance of stranded macro litter. We developed an object-oriented classification approach to automatically identify marine macro litter items in a UAS-based orthomosaic. A comparison is presented of three automated object-oriented machine learning (OOML) methods: random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and k-nearest neighbor (KNN). In general, detection performance was satisfactory for all three techniques, with mean F-scores of 65% for KNN, 68% for SVM, and 72% for RF. Comparison with manual detection showed that RF was the most accurate OOML macro litter detector, achieving the best overall detection quality (F-score) and the fewest false positives. However, because the number of tuning parameters differed across the three automated machine learning techniques and the three abundance maps correlated similarly with the manually produced abundance map, the simpler KNN classifier was preferred over the more complex RF. This study advances remote-sensing surveys of marine litter on coasts by optimizing automated detection on UAS-derived orthomosaics. MML abundance maps produced by UAS surveys help coastal managers and authorities in environmental pollution monitoring programs. They also support the search and evaluation of mitigation measures and improve clean-up operations in coastal environments.
